raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Removes four namespace aliases:

| Removed | Use instead |
| --- | --- |
| `cudnn.jax.grouped_gemm_swiglu` | `cudnn.grouped_gemm_swiglu_wrapper_sm100`, or `cudnn.grouped_gemm_glu_jax_sm100` with `act_func="swiglu"`, `generate_c=True`, and an FP8 `d_dtype` |
| `cudnn.jax.grouped_gemm_dswiglu` | `cudnn.grouped_gemm_dswiglu_wrapper_sm100`, or `cudnn.grouped_gemm_dglu_jax_sm100` with `act_func="dswiglu"` and an FP8 `d_dtype` |
| `cudnn.torch.grouped_gemm_swiglu` | `cudnn.grouped_gemm_swiglu_wrapper_sm100` (the same function) |
| `cudnn.torch.grouped_gemm_dswiglu` | `cudnn.grouped_gemm_dswiglu_wrapper_sm100` (the same function) |

This PR first deprecated them with a `FutureWarning`; it now removes them outright. They were added in #1079 and shipped in 1.30.0 and 1.31.0, the docs mark these APIs experimental, and no caller was found: TransformerEngine, FlashInfer, Megatron-LM and JAX (heads of 2026-10-12/13) do not reference any of the four, and GitHub code search finds no other user.

Changes:
- `cudnn.jax` / `cudnn.torch`: drop the names from `__all__` and `__getattr__`.
- `grouped_gemm_swiglu_wrapper_sm100` and `grouped_gemm_dswiglu_wrapper_sm100` used the `cudnn.jax` aliases for JAX inputs. They now import the JAX implementation directly, with the same CuTe DSL version check. Their behavior is unchanged.
- Error messages and a docstring that recommended the aliases now recommend the unified functions.
- API index: the four names are removed.
- Tests: `test_grouped_gemm_canonical_jax.py` calls the JAX implementation functions and the wrappers. `test_torch_namespace_alias_without_jax` becomes `test_torch_wrapper_without_jax`.
- Docs: the alias sections are removed from the two legacy pages and the overview. Each page keeps one line on what to call instead.

Testing, on an SM100 GPU with CUDA JAX 0.11.2:
- `test/python/gemm/jax/test_grouped_gemm_canonical_jax.py`: 117 passed, 0 skipped.
- Every other test file that imports `cudnn.jax` or `cudnn.torch`, plus the legacy grouped SwiGLU/dSwiGLU suites and the import-boundary tests: 423 passed, 202 skipped, 4 failed. The 4 failures are `sdpa/torch/test_torch_provider.py::test_sdpa_dense_parity`, which fail the same way on unmodified `develop` in this environment (see below).
- The API index scanner matches the edited baseline, apart from the environment artifact below.

Environment note: `develop`'s C++ does not build against the shared backend build on this machine, so the package under test was this branch's Python with a compiled module from an earlier build. That module lacks `_native_pack_from_facts` (the 4 SDPA failures) and the optional `gnn_agg_*` symbols (9 names in the index scan). This PR changes no C++.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `07a3d4c5a4ad` against base `b01222e76b23`.

No approval-blocking findings. The aliases still return the original callable implementations, the top-level wrappers avoid the deprecated namespace, and their existing DSL floor check is retained. The working legacy paths passed native SM100 validation. Please complete the migration instructions below so following the warning preserves the old defaults and outputs. Added cleanup/origin/module labels and project membership; the 1.32.0 milestone was already present. Thank you for your contribution!

**[P2] Include the compatibility arguments and output changes in the migration recipe** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/07a3d4c5a4ad68339c90caf714d0b66e44e32ff1/python/cudnn/jax/__init__.py#L62))

The suggested replacement is not equivalent with only act_func added. On the same valid canonical MXFP8 inputs, both old JAX aliases work with their default FP8 output, but the recommended unified functions default to BF16 and raise ValueError. After setting d_dtype explicitly, forward also needs generate_c=True to preserve the saved C used by backward; otherwise c_tensor becomes None. Backward adds a dbias_tensor entry, so six-value tuple unpacking also needs adjustment. Please link the warnings to a small migration example using explicit keyword arguments, the original FP8 dtype and generate_c=True for forward, and document the backward return-shape change. Test old versus migrated calls, including C and output keys, rather than only asserting the warning. The aliases themselves remain functional, so this is nonblocking.

Evidence: Independent SM100 probe: legacy forward/backward calls passed; name substitution plus act_func raised 'The MXFP8 JAX entry point requires FP8 output dtype' in both cases. Adding E4M3 dtype left forward C=None; adding generate_c=True restored byte parity for every shared output. The unified backward result has seven keys including dbias_tensor=None versus six legacy keys; shared results matched, with the existing dprob tolerance. Attribution: The replacement APIs' different contracts predate this PR; the incomplete deprecation/migration recommendation is new here.

Validation: Exact-source native SM100 canonical grouped JAX suite: 121 passed, no skips, including all four deprecation-warning cases, legacy wrappers, JIT/command-buffer execution and framework-isolation subprocesses. Independent migration probe exercised both legacy aliases and their recommended replacements. Explicit compatible arguments restored shared-output parity; repeated top-level JAX wrapper calls also passed with FutureWarning treated as an error. Marker-unfiltered API-index checks: 8 passed, 1 skipped, 13 subtests passed. Reviewed __all__, lazy module imports, stable callable identity and the retained DSL version checks; the public index file is unchanged.

Limitations: The local API-index runtime-baseline check skips outside its built-wheel qualification environment; this is not a wheel-release qualification. The kernels are unchanged. This review covers compatibility and migration behavior, not a new GPU performance or downstream training qualification. No additional broad CI was started: the default PR JAX lane's older DSL skips this canonical suite, whereas the compatible local environment above executed it.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `07a3d4c5a4ad` against base `b01222e76b23`.

No approval-blocking findings. The aliases still return the original callable implementations, the top-level wrappers avoid the deprecated namespace, and their existing DSL floor check is retained. The working legacy paths passed native SM100 validation. Please complete the migration instructions below so following the warning preserves the old defaults and outputs. Added cleanup/origin/module labels and project membership; the 1.32.0 milestone was already present. Thank you for your contribution!

**[P2] Include the compatibility arguments and output changes in the migration recipe** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/07a3d4c5a4ad68339c90caf714d0b66e44e32ff1/python/cudnn/jax/__init__.py#L62))

The suggested replacement is not equivalent with only act_func added. On the same valid canonical MXFP8 inputs, both old JAX aliases work with their default FP8 output, but the recommended unified functions default to BF16 and raise ValueError. After setting d_dtype explicitly, forward also needs generate_c=True to preserve the saved C used by backward; otherwise c_tensor becomes None. Backward adds a dbias_tensor entry, so six-value tuple unpacking also needs adjustment. Please link the warnings to a small migration example using explicit keyword arguments, the original FP8 dtype and generate_c=True for forward, and document the backward return-shape change. Test old versus migrated calls, including C and output keys, rather than only asserting the warning. The aliases themselves remain functional, so this is nonblocking.

Evidence: Independent SM100 probe: legacy forward/backward calls passed; name substitution plus act_func raised 'The MXFP8 JAX entry point requires FP8 output dtype' in both cases. Adding E4M3 dtype left forward C=None; adding generate_c=True restored byte parity for every shared output. The unified backward result has seven keys including dbias_tensor=None versus six legacy keys; shared results matched, with the existing dprob tolerance. Attribution: The replacement APIs' different contracts predate this PR; the incomplete deprecation/migration recommendation is new here.

Validation: Exact-source native SM100 canonical grouped JAX suite: 121 passed, no skips, including all four deprecation-warning cases, legacy wrappers, JIT/command-buffer execution and framework-isolation subprocesses. Independent migration probe exercised both legacy aliases and their recommended replacements. Explicit compatible arguments restored shared-output parity; repeated top-level JAX wrapper calls also passed with FutureWarning treated as an error. Marker-unfiltered API-index checks: 8 passed, 1 skipped, 13 subtests passed. Reviewed __all__, lazy module imports, stable callable identity and the retained DSL version checks; the public index file is unchanged.

Limitations: The local API-index runtime-baseline check skips outside its built-wheel qualification environment; this is not a wheel-release qualification. The kernels are unchanged. This review covers compatibility and migration behavior, not a new GPU performance or downstream training qualification. No additional broad CI was started: the default PR JAX lane's older DSL skips this canonical suite, whereas the compatible local environment above executed it.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
